rationale: Start with a broad mid-length scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the retention window across most of the solvent range. This should reveal whether early peaks are unretained or late peaks require stronger/faster elution, guiding the next narrowing or steepening step.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only improvement is to shorten t_last while keeping peaks inside the gradient. The first and last peaks correspond roughly to phi_e about 0.09 and 0.38, so a narrower, stronger-focused window with a shorter gradient should pull the late peak earlier without sacrificing resolution.

Since resolution is comfortably complete, the main lever left is temperature: increasing T should reduce retention across the board and may bring the last peak under 10 minutes while likely preserving adequate separation. This also tests whether selectivity changes at higher temperature threaten the currently generous minimum resolution.

At 60 C all pairs still clear 1.5, so a modestly steeper gradient should shorten the run further and may bring the last peak below 10 minutes. The current weakest pair is only 1.83, so this is a cautious compression rather than an aggressive one.

The 16 min gradient crossed the 10 min target but over-compressed the critical 4/5 pair, while 20 min had full resolution but t_last slightly too long. An intermediate tG of 18 min should recover enough resolution for that pair while likely keeping the last peak near or under 10 minutes.

The limiting issue is the 4/5 pair, which improved strongly when temperature dropped from 60 to 40 C, while t_last worsened. A small step down to 55 C should boost that pair just enough to reach full resolution, and with the 18 min gradient may still keep the last peak very close to 10 minutes for a near-optimal tradeoff.

The weakest pair switched from 4/5 at 60 C to 6/7 at 55 C, indicating a selectivity crossover with temperature; 50 C may place both pairs above 1.5. Keeping tG at 18 preserves the near-optimal run length while probing the temperature sweet spot for full resolution.

At 55 C the critical 6/7 pair is already much better than at 50 C, and lengthening from 18 to 20 min should specifically help that slope-sensitive region while preserving acceptable resolution elsewhere. This tests whether a slightly shallower gradient can lift the 6/7 pair above 1.5 without pushing the last peak too far past 10 minutes.

The 4/5 pair is the only limitation at 60 C, and it improved from R 1.05 to 1.44 when tG increased from 16 to 18 min, suggesting it is strongly slope-sensitive. Extrapolating one more step to 22 min at the same temperature may push that pair above 1.5, trading a small time penalty for full resolution and potentially the best CRF so far.

The last peak is well after the gradient ends, so reducing phi1 slightly should barely affect total run time while changing selectivity near the middle of the gradient, where the limiting 4/5 pair elutes. This tests whether a small window shift can lift that pair above 1.5 without losing the near-10-minute last peak.

Compared with 0.95, lowering phi1 to 0.90 improved the critical 4/5 pair but delayed the last peak; shortening tG should recover that time while keeping the beneficial selectivity shift. This probes whether a narrower, slightly steeper window can get both full resolution and t_last near 10 minutes.

The best CRF sits at the edge where pair 4/5 is just under full credit and the last peak is just over 10 minutes; raising phi1 from 0.85 to 0.90 at the same tG may pull the last peak slightly earlier while keeping similar selectivity. This is a nearby grid point with a plausible chance to improve the time term more than it hurts the limiting pair.

The 0.85–16 min and 0.95–18 min runs gave identical results, implying the effective gradient seen by the analytes is dominated by the same early-mid composition range. Extending tG to 18 min at phi1 0.85 should specifically ease the critical 4/5 pair while likely moving t_last only modestly, giving a realistic shot at full resolution with minimal time penalty.

The best point is constrained by pair 4/5, and lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved that pair while increasing retention; moving one more step lower may push 4/5 to full credit. Keeping tG at 16 offsets the expected retention increase so the last peak may stay near 10 minutes.

Lowering phi1 continues to help the critical 4/5 pair, so the next step is to compress the gradient in time to counter the retention increase and target t_last near 10 minutes. This nearby point tests whether stronger selectivity improvement can be kept while maintaining a favorable time term.

Several methods with the same gradient slope appear to give nearly identical chromatograms, so the dominant control is likely b rather than the absolute window endpoints. Testing phi1 0.80 at 14 min keeps nearly the same late-gradient strength but slightly alters the composition profile around the critical 4/5 region, which could nudge that pair over 1.5 while keeping t_last close to 10 minutes.

Results suggest iso-slope conditions track closely, with the best points all near the same gradient steepness and pair 4/5 remaining just short of full credit. Lowering phi1 another step at the same tG changes the composition where 4/5 elute without increasing steepness, giving one more chance to improve that pair while keeping the last peak near the 10-minute target.

The 50–55 C region caused a severe selectivity collapse for pair 6/7, so mapping one more lower-temperature point will define whether 40–45 C offers a different fully resolved selectivity pattern that might support later time optimization. This is an information-rich check of the temperature response because 60 C appears stuck near a CRF ceiling around 0.986.

Since all analytes are well retained above dead time, this is a low-risk way to probe for a small time gain near the current optimum.

The data strongly suggest many conditions collapse onto similar behavior when the effective slope is similar, and the best CRF lies near the boundary where 4/5 is just under 1.5 and t_last just over 10 minutes. This slightly steeper, lower-phi1 run targets a small time gain while preserving the favorable low-phi1 selectivity that kept 4/5 above 1.5 at 0.70/14.

The 0.70/14 run fully resolved all pairs but paid only a modest time penalty, so moving one step lower in phi1 at the same tG may further help the critical 4/5 pair while keeping t_last close enough to 10 minutes to remain competitive. This is a targeted test of whether the 4/5 selectivity keeps improving as the window shifts lower.

The best region is clearly around the 0.70–0.95 window and 14–18 min, with pair 4/5 sitting right below full credit at several conditions. This midpoint test between the tied best methods may reveal a small nonlinearity in selectivity versus phi1 at similar steepness and has one of the last realistic chances to nudge 4/5 above 1.5 without adding much time.

The 0.65/14 run gave full resolution but too much time penalty, so shortening to 12 min is the direct test of whether that improved 4/5 selectivity can be retained while bringing the last peak closer to 10 minutes. With only a few injections left, this is the most informative remaining neighbor of the best-performing region.

Several runs indicate the chromatogram is effectively controlled by gradient slope, with tied-best performance recurring along an iso-slope line; this point continues that line while shifting the phi window lower around the critical 4/5 elution zone. It is one of the few untested neighbors that could still move 4/5 slightly above 1.5 without worsening the already near-optimal run time.

The last remaining useful test is to continue the same lower-phi window trend but shorten the gradient one more step, aiming to preserve the improved 4/5 selectivity seen at phi1 0.60 while pulling t_last closer to 10 minutes. This is the best untried compromise near the apparent tradeoff frontier.
